newsitem.title: USA: Worldcom invests $300 mln in UUNET network.
newsitem.headline: Worldcom invests $300 mln in UUNET network.

text.p: Worldcom Inc said Wednesday it plans to spend about $300 million to expand the network of UUNET Technologies Inc, an Internet services provider and Worldcom subsidiary.
The expansion and upgrade will more than quadruple UUNET's available capacity in terms of both backbone bandwidth and dial capacity, Worldcom said.
John Sidgmore, president and chief executive of UUNET, said the expansion plan is unprecedented in scope and schedule.

"The pace of growth in the Internet underscores the importance of ISPs being facilities-based. The recent merger with WorldCom gives UUNET the ability to secure and control the bandwidth necessary to meet our customers' requirements for high-performance service," he said.

Over the next six months, UUNET will implement a migration of its backbone segments to support the highest speed available for Internet Protocol transmission, OC12, at 622 million bits per second. The company said it will migrate the backbone links to the ATM, or Asynchronous Transfer Mode, protocol.

The company said it will install new generation, high density MAX TNT remote access concentrators throughout the United States, Canada and Puerto Rico. The concentrators, from Ascend Communications Inc, support both analog and digital dial-up traffic.

UUNET Technologies has about 50,000 business customers worldwide. It is the official Internet access provider to the Microsoft Network and also supports GTE, EarthLink Networks, WebTV Networks Inc and several other providers.
